transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my eating has gotten really out of hand, especially in the evenings. I’ll leave work and tell myself I’m just picking up dinner, but then I’ll end up buying, like, a family-size takeout order—way more than one person needs—and then I’ll stop at the store too and get chips or bakery things, like pastries or cookies or whatever looks good in the moment.

And then I get home and it’s like I just… start eating, and I don’t even really register how much is disappearing until most of it is gone. It’s embarrassing to say, but I can eat the majority of all of that by myself before it even hits me. I’ll look at the containers or the empty bag and think, “How did I do that again?” So, yeah, that’s why I’m here. It’s been scaring me a little.
How often do these episodes of eating large amounts of food happen?

It’s… pretty frequent. I started trying to write it down in a journal because I honestly didn’t trust my memory about it, and when I look back, there’s barely been a week in the last several months where it didn’t happen at least once. And most weeks it’s not just once—it’s several nights.

I think I was telling myself it was more occasional than it really was, but seeing it written down made it harder to explain away.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating large amounts of food?

Yes. Very much, honestly. It’s not just like, “Oh, I ate too much, I’ll do better tomorrow.” It feels like this heavy shame that just sits on me afterward. I’ll be looking at the wrappers or the takeout containers, and I feel embarrassed even though no one else is there to see it.

And it affects what I do afterward, too. I’ve stopped inviting people over because I’m afraid they’ll notice things, or I just feel too ashamed to have anyone in my space after I’ve done that. Even little routines I used to count on in the evening—like yoga, or going out to do gardening chores—I’ll skip them because I’m so preoccupied with what happened. I just kind of shut down and don’t want to be seen.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these episodes?

Yes. That’s probably the part that scares me the most, honestly. It’s not just that I decide to eat too much and then regret it. It feels like once I start, there’s this awful switch that flips, and even while it’s happening I can be thinking, Taylor, put it away, stop opening things, you don’t need any more, and my hands just… keep going.

Like I’ll tell myself, “Okay, just finish this one thing and then close the container,” but then I’m already reaching for something else. Or I’ll stand up like I’m going to put it away, and somehow I end up taking it back with me. It feels almost automatic, like I’m watching myself do it and I’m not the one in charge. That sounds dramatic, but that is really what it feels like in the moment. I can be completely aware that I want to stop, and still not be able to make myself stop.
Do these episodes of eating large amounts of food usually happen at night, or do they also occur during the day?

I’m not completely sure I’ve tracked that part carefully enough. I mean, when I think of them, I picture nighttime because that’s when I’m usually alone and everything is quiet, so those stand out more in my mind. But I don’t want to say they only happen at night, because I haven’t really been paying attention to the time of day in a precise way.

In the journal I was mostly writing down that it happened, not always when it happened. So… I guess the honest answer is that I don’t know if there’s a strict pattern. Night is what I notice more, but I’m not sure I could say it never happens during the day.
Do you feel like you're eating very quickly during these episodes?

Yes. Very quickly. Faster than I think I even realize in the moment.

It’s like I’m not sitting down and enjoying food the way a normal meal would be. A lot of times I’m standing at the dining room table, with the microwave going or still warm, and there are boxes or containers around me, and I’m just… eating. One bite is barely swallowed before I’m already reaching for the next thing. I don’t really taste it after the first bite or two. It’s more like I’m trying to get it in before I can think too much, if that makes sense.

And afterward I’ll sometimes remember it in these little flashes—like opening something, heating something, taking another bite—but I don’t remember actually savoring it. It feels rushed, almost frantic. Like my body is ahead of my brain.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, partly because I kind of avoid the scale. I know that probably sounds evasive, but it’s more that I don’t want to see the number and then have it ruin my whole day.

My clothes feel different sometimes, but I can’t say whether that’s a “significant” change or just me being more aware of my body. Some days things feel tighter, and then other days I tell myself maybe I’m imagining it or maybe it’s bloating or just the way something was washed. So I don’t think I can give you a clear number or even a confident yes or no.

If you mean, like, have I noticed a dramatic change over the past few months, I don’t know that I can say that. I just haven’t kept track in a way that would make me sure.
Do you enjoy the taste of the food while you're eating during these episodes?

Not really, no. I mean, maybe the first bite, if it’s something I’d normally like, I might notice it for a second. But once I’m in that… whatever that mode is, I’m eating so fast that I barely taste anything.

It’s not like sitting down with a plate and thinking, “This is good.” It’s more like I’m standing there at the dining room table, the microwave still going or something still hot from it, and there are boxes or containers around me, and I’m just moving from one thing to the next. I’ll be swallowing one bite while my hand is already reaching for the next. So the taste kind of disappears. It’s just getting it down quickly. I don’t feel like I’m enjoying it in the normal way.
Do you often criticize yourself after these episodes of eating?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I’m not sure I would call it “criticize,” exactly, because it’s not always like I’m sitting there making a list of insults at myself or anything that organized.

I do usually feel bad afterward, though. Like there’s this heavy feeling of, “Why did I do that?” or “What was that about?” But whether that counts as criticizing myself, I’m not sure. Sometimes it’s more just embarrassment or wanting to avoid thinking about it. I’ll kind of clean up or put things away and try to act like it didn’t happen, even to myself.

So… yes and no, I guess. I don’t know if I’m using the right words. I don’t always notice exactly what I’m saying to myself afterward, but it definitely doesn’t feel kind.
Do you often think very negatively about yourself after these episodes of eating?

I’m not sure I can separate that from what I already said, if that makes sense. “Very negatively” feels like a strong phrase, and I don’t know if I’m always aware of the exact words in my head afterward.

Sometimes it’s less like a clear thought and more like this… sinking feeling. Like I don’t want to be in my own skin for a minute, or I don’t want to look too closely at what just happened. I might think something like, “Why can’t I just be normal about this?” but then I try to shut it down pretty quickly because if I stay with it, it feels awful.

So, I guess there are negative thoughts, yes, but I don’t know how to measure whether they’re “very” negative or how often. I’m not sitting there calmly evaluating myself afterward. It’s more messy than that. I usually just want to move on and not think about it.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these episodes?

Yes. That’s probably the worst part of it, honestly. It really does feel like I’m not in control once it starts.

I can be standing there, and part of me is completely aware of what’s happening. Like I’ll have this thought, almost like I’m talking to myself: “Taylor, stop. Put it away. Close the container. Walk away.” And then my hands are still doing the opposite. I’m opening another container, or going back to the bag, or getting something else out, even while I’m thinking I don’t want to keep doing this.

It feels like this awful switch flips. Before it starts, I might have some choice, or at least it feels like I do. But once I cross that line, it’s like the reasonable part of me is watching from a few steps back, trying to get my attention, and my body just keeps going. I know that probably sounds strange, because of course it’s still me doing it, but in the moment it honestly doesn’t feel like I’m the one in charge.
Do you usually feel uncomfortably full after these episodes of eating?

Yes… usually, yes. I wish I could say I stop before that point, but a lot of the time I don’t.

It’s not just “full” like after a big dinner. It’s more like my stomach feels tight, like stretched tight, and sometimes it actually hurts. And even then, I don’t always stop at the first sign of that feeling. I keep going past where any reasonable person would say, “Okay, that’s enough.” Then afterward I’m just sitting there kind of frozen on the couch, trying not to move too much because moving makes me feel worse.

There have been times where even the idea of walking upstairs feels uncomfortable, like I’m aware of every step because my stomach feels so heavy and painful. So yes, uncomfortably full is definitely the right phrase. It’s embarrassing to admit, but that’s usually how far it goes.
Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t… I don’t think I do those things in a deliberate way, like a planned “now I have to undo it” kind of way.

Vomiting, no, that’s not something I make myself do. Laxatives… no, not as a regular thing or as some kind of compensation. And with exercise, I mean, I can get into a mindset where I think, “I should move more,” or “I need to get back on track,” but I wouldn’t say I go exercise excessively right after to make up for it. At least not in the way I think you mean.

Mostly what happens afterward is more like I feel awful and uncomfortable and embarrassed, and I sort of retreat. I might tell myself I’ll be stricter later or do better tomorrow, but I don’t usually turn around and do something drastic like vomiting or laxatives. So… no, I don’t think so.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without feeling guilty or ashamed afterward?

I mean… the large amount part, yes, absolutely. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came in.

It’s usually in the evenings. I’ll stop and get takeout, but not just like a normal dinner. It’ll be more like a family-size order, something that’s clearly meant for more than one person, and then I’ll still go into the store and add chips or bakery things or whatever looks good in the moment. And then I get home and eat most of it myself, sometimes before I even really seem to register how much is gone.

It’s strange because if you put it all out on the counter at the beginning, it would look like too much. Like, I know that. But in the moment it doesn’t land that way. I’ll just keep going from one thing to the next, and then suddenly I notice the containers are almost empty or the bag is mostly gone, and I’m like… how did I get here again?

So yes, I do have episodes where I eat a really large amount in a short time. The “without feeling guilty or ashamed” part is harder for me to say yes to, because it’s not like I’m relaxed and fine afterward. But the eating a lot, quickly, mostly by myself before it fully sinks in — yes, that happens.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel okay about it afterward?

No… I don’t think I ever really feel okay about it afterward. Or if there’s a moment where I feel numb, it’s not “okay” exactly. It’s more like I’m kind of checked out for a little while.

If I’ve eaten what I know is a lot in a short amount of time, I usually don’t sit there feeling satisfied like, “That was nice, I enjoyed that.” It’s more complicated and heavier than that. Even if the food tasted good at the beginning, afterward I’m usually aware of what just happened, and I start going over it in my head. Like, why did I do that again, why couldn’t I stop earlier, why did I buy all that in the first place.

So no, I wouldn’t say I feel okay afterward. Maybe during the first few minutes I’m not fully thinking about it, but once it catches up with me, I don’t feel fine about it.
Do you find that you're not really interested in the food itself when you're having one of these episodes of eating a large amount?

Yeah… I think that’s true a lot of the time. Not completely at the very beginning maybe, because sometimes I do want a specific thing, or it sounds good when I’m buying it. But once I’m actually in it, it’s not like I’m sitting down and enjoying a meal.

I’ll be standing at the dining room table with the boxes and wrappers around me, and the microwave going or just finished, and I’m eating so fast that I barely taste anything. It’s almost mechanical. I’ll take a bite and before I’ve even really swallowed it, I’m already reaching for the next thing, opening another container, grabbing another handful, whatever it is.

And afterward I’ll realize I don’t even remember what half of it tasted like. I remember the motion of it more than the food, if that makes sense. Like standing there, going from one thing to the next, swallowing quickly, not really pausing. So yes, during those episodes, the food itself almost becomes secondary. It’s not like normal eating where I’m paying attention to flavor or whether I’m enjoying it. It’s just… fast. Too fast.
Have you noticed any significant weight gain since these episodes of eating large amounts of food started?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean, I haven’t been tracking it in a very organized way, so I don’t want to say a number and be wrong.

I’ve noticed my clothes feel different sometimes, and I get nervous stepping on a scale, so I tend to avoid it. But whether it’s been a “significant” amount since these episodes started… I don’t really know. It’s hard for me to separate what’s actually changed from what I’m afraid has changed, if that makes sense.

So I guess the most honest answer is: I’m not sure. I haven’t been keeping close enough track to say clearly.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after one of these episodes of eating?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that clearly. I don’t think I have a specific answer I can give you, like something I know for sure and can point to. It’s not something I’ve been keeping track of in that way.

After those episodes I usually feel upset and uncomfortable, and I may kind of shut down or just want to avoid thinking about it, but as far as making myself vomit… I’m not sure how to say it. I don’t have a clear “yes, this is something I do” answer. If you mean deliberately going and forcing it afterward, I don’t think that’s been a regular thing I can describe. I’m sorry, I know that’s probably not as direct as you’re asking, but I don’t want to say something inaccurate.
Have you ever made yourself vomit after eating a large amount of food?

I know you asked that a moment ago, and I’m trying not to be evasive. I just… I don’t have a clean yes-or-no answer that feels accurate.

I don’t think of myself as someone who makes myself vomit after eating a lot. Like, that’s not something I can say I routinely do or that I have a clear pattern of doing. Afterward I can feel really uncomfortable and ashamed, and sometimes I just want to get away from the feeling of it, but if you’re asking specifically whether I go and deliberately force myself to throw up, I don’t have a definite example I can point to and say, “Yes, that’s what I do.”

So I guess my answer is no, not that I’m aware of in any regular or clear way… but I’m also a little hesitant because these episodes are embarrassing and I don’t always think clearly afterward. I don’t want to give you the wrong impression.

And even then, I don’t always stop at the first sign of that feeling. I keep going past where any reasonable person would say, “Okay, that’s enough.” Then afterward I’m just sitting there kind of frozen on the couch, trying not to move too much because moving makes me feel worse.

There have been times where even the idea of walking upstairs feels uncomfortable, like I’m aware of every step because my stomach feels so heavy and painful. So yes, uncomfortably full is definitely the right phrase. It’s embarrassing to admit, but that’s usually how far it goes.

doctor.question: Do you ever try to make up for these episodes of eating by doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t… I don’t think I do those things in a deliberate way, like a planned “now I have to undo it” kind of way.

Vomiting, no, that’s not something I make myself do. Laxatives… no, not as a regular thing or as some kind of compensation. And with exercise, I mean, I can get into a mindset where I think, “I should move more,” or “I need to get back on track,” but I wouldn’t say I go exercise excessively right after to make up for it. At least not in the way I think you mean.

Mostly what happens afterward is more like I feel awful and uncomfortable and embarrassed, and I sort of retreat. I might tell myself I’ll be stricter later or do better tomorrow, but I don’t usually turn around and do something drastic like vomiting or laxatives. So… no, I don’t think so.

doctor.intent: determine presence of binge eating episodes without guilt or shame
doctor.question: Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without feeling guilty or ashamed afterward?

patient.answer:
I mean… the large amount part, yes, absolutely. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came in.

It’s usually in the evenings. I’ll stop and get takeout, but not just like a normal dinner. It’ll be more like a family-size order, something that’s clearly meant for more than one person, and then I’ll still go into the store and add chips or bakery things or whatever looks good in the moment. And then I get home and eat most of it myself, sometimes before I even really seem to register how much is gone.

It’s strange because if you put it all out on the counter at the beginning, it would look like too much. Like, I know that. But in the moment it doesn’t land that way. I’ll just keep going from one thing to the next, and then suddenly I notice the containers are almost empty or the bag is mostly gone, and I’m like… how did I get here again?

So yes, I do have episodes where I eat a really large amount in a short time. The “without feeling guilty or ashamed” part is harder for me to say yes to, because it’s not like I’m relaxed and fine afterward. doctor.intent: determine presence of binge eating episodes without guilt
doctor.question: Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and feel okay about it afterward?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically asking whether I feel okay afterward, meaning absence of guilt, shame, or distress after eating. The provided symptom profile does not include a dedicated item for post-episode guilt, shame, or feeling okay afterward.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think I ever really feel okay about it afterward. Or if there’s a moment where I feel numb, it’s not “okay” exactly. It’s more like I’m kind of checked out for a little while.

If I’ve eaten what I know is a lot in a short amount of time, I usually don’t sit there feeling satisfied like, “That was nice, I enjoyed that.” It’s more complicated and heavier than that. Even if the food tasted good at the beginning, afterward I’m usually aware of what just happened, and I start going over it in my head. Like, why did I do that again, why couldn’t I stop earlier, why did I buy all that in the first place.

So no, I wouldn’t say I feel okay afterward. Maybe during the first few minutes I’m not fully thinking about it, but once it catches up with me, I don’t feel fine about it.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think that’s true a lot of the time. Not completely at the very beginning maybe, because sometimes I do want a specific thing, or it sounds good when I’m buying it. But once I’m actually in it, it’s not like I’m sitting down and enjoying a meal.

I’ll be standing at the dining room table with the boxes and wrappers around me, and the microwave going or just finished, and I’m eating so fast that I barely taste anything. It’s almost mechanical. I’ll take a bite and before I’ve even really swallowed it, I’m already reaching for the next thing, opening another container, grabbing another handful, whatever it is.

And afterward I’ll realize I don’t even remember what half of it tasted like. I remember the motion of it more than the food, if that makes sense. Like standing there, going from one thing to the next, swallowing quickly, not really pausing. So yes, during those episodes, the food itself almost becomes secondary. It’s not like normal eating where I’m paying attention to flavor or whether I’m enjoying it. It’s just… fast. Too fast.
